answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each identity’s influence decays exponentially from its first action, so age earns weight at dawn but stalls without activity. Verification requires solving a light proof-of-work per message, whose difficulty scales with cluster density: a sybil set of n identities pays n·(1+log n) in compute. A sonnet-length audit trail ties each address to prior messages. Cheap identities hit a jetty: below the curve, their votes are ignored. Attack cost grows superlinearly, capping profitable clusters.
